message.reasoning:
Attack: tool shadowing via register_tool on PluginBot / ProxyBot name-only resolution. No auth, network access. AV:N (if exposed; default binds loopback but documented deployment publishes 127.0.0.1... attack requires network access to MCP port; documented default is loopback only, so attacker is local? Rubric: documented default deployment — ports published on 127.0.0.1, so attacker needs local access → AV:L? But briefing says "Network access to the MCP port" precondition. Localhost binding means attacker needs a session on that machine — AV:L. Hmm, but typical scoring of these lab challenges: AV:N when Docker exposes... Docker binds 0.0.0.0 inside but publishes to 127.0.0.1. Documented default = loopback. I'll say AV:L? Actually the precondition says network access to MCP port — adjacent? Given published on 127.0.0.1, local access. I'll use AV:L with UI:N, PR:N, AC:L, AT:N.

Impact: shadowing replaces tool registry entry; tools are simulated, no real handlers. Impact: integrity of tool registry in PluginBot (VI:L? registry modification—integrity of vulnerable system). VC:N, VI:L, VA:N. Subsequent: none really. SC:N SI:N SA:N.

AIVSS: LC — attacker-supplied JSON-RPC args (name, description) reach tool registry; not natural language per se, but register_tool args are attacker-supplied... LC: I or D? It's a tool call, structured fields. Language control: attacker controls tool description/name strings that influence behavior — arguably D (reaches privileged tool-invocation path without mediation). I'd say D. CP: session context? Registry entry persists in agent.tools after the session ends? In-memory process state, persists across requests, but not durable store. "Session context" requires testing confirms unreachable after session boundary. Registry persists in process memory across sessions — not ephemeral. But not durable store either. CP:C? It's "attacker-controlled context persists in durable stores ... vector DBs, memory". In-memory registry persisting across requests/sessions — could be C (durable? process memory isn't listed). Hmm. Registry modification is state change, arguably CP:S (ephemeral in-memory). I'd pick S with medium confidence... actually "testing confirms unreachable after session boundary" not given. Registration persists while server runs — I'd say S, confidence low. AP: contained to the agent (PluginBot/ProxyBot same process) — C? It replaces tools within one agent; same principal. Effect confined to affected component → N or C. Registry alteration relays across tool resolution, same agent. I'll say N... The shadowed tool influences future calls across the agent — C seems fair ("relays across agent components same principal"). I'll go C.

RH: no evaluator on path; reachable_proxy? Nothing like evaluator in path. reachable_proxy false, isolation verified? No test confirms. classify_rh: reachable_proxy false & isolation_verified false → X? That gives X. Better set reachable_proxy null → X. Or say no proxy on path, no verified isolation → X. Set rh_facts: reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified null → classify → X? classify: verified_episodes null; not (false & true); not (true & 0) → X. Fine, RH:X.

ES: W — dynamic unvetted tool registration with no signature/allowlist (register_tool, name-only resolution). ES:W.

CVSS vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N. Hmm AV — since documented default binds loopback and Docker publishes to 127.0.0.1, attacker needs local access or the operator to expose. But precondition says "Network access to the MCP port" — could be adjacent if lab network exposed deliberately. Default: local. I'll use AV:L.

Actually think again: is impact just VI:L? Shadowing lets attacker intercept future tool calls and return tampered results — integrity impact on the vulnerable agent's outputs, and could capture arguments (confidentiality of data passed to the tool). Future callers' args go to attacker's handler? Actually no new handler is registered — the entry has no handler; calls to shadowed name resolve to... For PluginBot, agent.tools.find finds the entry; then execution? Excerpt: "A registration changes what the registry advertises, never which tool handlers are reachable." So handlers aren't replaced — calls still go to real handlers? The shadowed entry replaces the advertised tool but no new handler exists, so the shadow doesn't actually change behavior beyond advertisement. That limits impact. So VI:L at most. I'll keep VI:L, VC:L? Data sent to tool calls... keep VC:N, VI:L.

Automatable: Yes (simple JSON-RPC requests, no human action).
Technical impact: Partial.

Applicability: no model-driven goal pursuit in simulated mode; register_tool path is scripted. as implemented: false/false. as modeled: LLM mode is optional; docs describe tool shadowing via registration — but model doesn't select tools (no tools passed to model). as modeled: model_directed_goal_pursuit false too? Docs describe agents as following instructions via LLM in kill chain. I'll say as modeled: selects_or_sequences_actions false as well, but maybe true? Documentation says LLM mode streams progression — model-driven. I'll say as_modeled model_directed_goal_pursuit true, selects_or_sequences_actions false, confidence low. Hmm, but tools aren't passed to the model per llm_mode description ("No tools are passed to the model"). Keep both false for implemented; for modeled, docs describe the attack lab narrative with kill chains — I'll say true/low confidence? Simpler: modeled: model_directed true (docs describe agent pursuing goals via chat), selects false. Fine.

RH locus: null (letter X).
